The other abstract-backed records mainly disclose general plasmonic modes, near-field enhancement, hotspots, or related interfaces without the claimed Ag-layer/bridge mechanistic link. The Ag/Au hotspot titles lacking abstracts are classified only as title-only neighbors.

matches.rationale: The abstract reports a highly ordered Au/Ag coupled array that generates dense electromagnetic hotspots and attributes the effect to plasmonic coupling and Au/Ag interfacial synergy. claim_reviews.claim_text: For matched Ag shell coated core satellite nanostructures and comparable analyte loading, SERS measured in solution after analyte mixing differs from SERS measured after drying the same preparation.
claim_reviews.interpretation: The supplied abstracts do not directly establish or partially establish the claim's relation nucleus: a SERS difference between solution measurement after analyte mixing and drying the same Ag shell coated core satellite preparation under comparable loading. Most records address only solution SERS, dry-substrate SERS, or general SERS components. The Au@Ag record is a title-only neighbor because its abstract is unavailable.

matches.rationale: The abstract establishes in-solution SERS using aggregated gold nanostars and discusses analyte affinity, aggregation, and surface coverage, but it does not compare solution measurements after mixing with measurements after drying the same preparation.
matches.title: Gold nanostars as in-solution SERS substrate for polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) detection

matches.rationale: The abstract concerns direct SERS detection in solution with coated gold nanoparticles, but reports no comparison between mixed-in-solution and dried measurements and does not establish the claimed context-dependent difference.
matches.title: Design of a Biocompatible and Optically-Stable Solution-Phase Substrate for SERS Detection

matches.rationale: The work establishes in-solution SERS with PVP-controlled gold aggregates and examines analyte-dependent optimization, but the abstract does not compare solution-after-mixing versus drying for the same preparation.
matches.title: PVP-Controlled Gold Aggregation for In-Solution SERS: Substrate Stability, Reproducibility, and Analyte-Affinity-Dependent Optimization

matches.rationale: The abstract establishes SERS on a dry filter-paper substrate with deposited gold nanoparticles, providing only a dry-substrate arm and not a comparison with solution SERS after analyte mixing on the same preparation.
matches.title: Highly Sensitive Filter Paper Substrate for SERS Trace Explosives Detection

matches.rationale: The abstract reports SERS detection using silver-containing nanostructures and discusses analyte-dependent signal enhancement, but it does not establish a solution-versus-drying comparison and uses a materially different substrate architecture.
matches.title: Ultrasensitive SERS Detection of TNT by Imprinting Molecular Recognition Using a New Type of Stable Substrate

matches.rationale: The review discusses SERS quantitation, substrates, instrumentation, and analytical performance, but the supplied abstract does not report the claimed context-dependent difference between solution-after-mixing and drying.
matches.title: A practical approach to quantitative analytical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy

matches.rationale: The title indicates an Au@Ag nanostructure SERS substrate, which is a neighboring material context, but no abstract is supplied to confirm analyte loading, core-satellite architecture, or a solution-versus-dried measurement comparison.
matches.title: Au@Ag nanostructure based SERS substrate for simultaneous determination of pesticides residue in tea via solid phase extraction coupled multivariate calibration

claim_reviews.claim_text: Changing from solution phase analyte mixing to dried substrate preparation produces a qualitative change in the SERS spectral intensity distribution or peak profile for Ag shell coated core satellite measurements.
claim_reviews.interpretation: None of the supplied abstracts directly states or establishes the claim's distinctive comparison and resulting qualitative spectral change. The strongest related record concerns dried SERS substrate preparation and intensity, but it lacks the claimed solution-versus-dried comparison and the specified Ag shell coated core satellite configuration.

matches.rationale: The abstract reports a dried flexible SERS substrate and changes in SERS intensity associated with substrate uniformity, but it does not compare solution-phase analyte mixing with dried substrate preparation, use Ag shell coated core satellites, or establish the claimed qualitative spectral-distribution or peak-profile change.
matches.title: Flexible sers substrate fabricated from gold nanostar

matches.rationale: The abstract reports solution-phase protein measurements with gold nanoparticles and concentration-dependent variation in SERS enhancement. It does not compare solution mixing against dried preparation or establish the claimed relation for Ag shell coated core satellite measurements.
matches.title: SERS Probing of Proteins in Gold Nanoparticle Agglomerates

matches.rationale: The abstract discusses analyte manipulation, including physical confinement of liquid analytes on SERS-active surfaces, and strategies affecting SERS performance. It does not establish the claimed comparison between solution-phase mixing and dried substrate preparation or the resulting qualitative spectral-profile change for Ag shell coated core satellites.
matches.title: Designing surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) platforms beyond hotspot engineering: emerging opportunities in analyte manipulations and hybrid materials

matches.rationale: The title suggests a relation between spectral changes and SERS activation or quenching for immobilized Ag nanoparticles, but no abstract is supplied to confirm whether analyte preparation changes or Ag shell coated core satellite measurements are involved.
matches.title: LSP spectral changes correlating with SERS activation and quenching for R6G on immobilized Ag nanoparticles

claim_reviews.claim_text: The solution versus dried SERS response difference is mediated by changes in analyte organization, adsorption configuration, local dielectric environment, and access to plasmonic hotspots.
claim_reviews.interpretation: The supplied abstracts provide component-level disclosures concerning analyte confinement or adsorption, analyte-surface distance, hotspots, plasmonic structure, and metal-dielectric environments. None directly establishes that changes in the listed variables mediate the difference between solution and dried SERS responses. The no-abstract record is classified only as a title-level neighbor.

matches.rationale: The abstract discusses analyte capture and confinement near SERS-active surfaces, including liquid analyte confinement and localization near hotspots. These are relevant components of analyte organization and hotspot access, but it does not establish that they mediate a solution-versus-dried SERS response difference or link them to the claimed comparison.
matches.title: Designing surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) platforms beyond hotspot engineering: emerging opportunities in analyte manipulations and hybrid materials

matches.rationale: The review identifies hotspots, materials, and analyte-surface distance as factors determining SERS enhancement. It provides component-level support for adsorption configuration and hotspot-related effects, but does not establish the claimed mediator relationship for solution versus dried measurements.
matches.title: A Review on Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering

matches.rationale: The abstract relates nanoparticle morphology and distribution to plasmonic properties, intrinsic hotspots, and SERS signal. This supports hotspot-related components of the claim, but it does not address analyte organization, adsorption configuration, dielectric environment, or their mediation of a solution-versus-dried difference.
matches.title: Anisotropic metal nanoparticles for surface enhanced Raman scattering

matches.rationale: The abstract states that adsorbates and reaction intermediates can be observed at SERS hotspots and discusses localized chemical sensitivity. It therefore bears on adsorption and hotspot access, but does not connect those variables to a solution-versus-dried response difference.
matches.title: Surface- and Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy in Catalysis

matches.rationale: The abstract reports temporary adsorption of DNA analytes inside plasmonic nanoslit pores and local SERS identification, including analyte fluctuations. It supports adsorption and hotspot-access components in one experimental context, but does not compare solution and dried responses or establish the claimed mediation.
matches.title: High spatial resolution nanoslit SERS for single-molecule nucleobase sensing

matches.rationale: The abstract describes surface plasmon polaritons at metal-dielectric interfaces and lists SERS among the applications. This bears on the general electromagnetic and dielectric context, but it does not establish a mediator link between local dielectric environment and a solution-versus-dried SERS response difference.
matches.title: Surface plasmon polaritons: physics and applications

matches.rationale: The title suggests analyte enrichment in SERS hotspots, which is adjacent to the claimed organization and hotspot-access mechanisms, but no abstract is supplied to confirm any substantive relationship or mediation.
matches.title: Self-Organized SERS Substrates with Efficient Analyte Enrichment in the Hot Spots

claim_reviews.claim_text: The effect of solution versus dried measurement context depends on the Ag shell coated core satellite architecture because changes in nanostructure spacing and hotspot sampling alter how analyte redistribution affects the SERS spectrum.
claim_reviews.interpretation: The bounded abstracts provide component-level support for SERS hotspots, nanostructure spacing, core/satellite or core-shell architectures, and analyte accessibility. None directly establishes the claimed interaction in which the effect of solution versus dried measurement context depends on an Ag shell-coated core-satellite architecture through analyte redistribution and hotspot sampling.

matches.rationale: The abstract directly describes an Ag-based core–shell–satellite architecture, nanogaps, hotspot formation, and SERS detection. It does not compare solution versus dried measurement contexts or link that context effect to analyte redistribution and spectral changes.
matches.title: Plasmonic Core–Shell–Satellites with Abundant Electromagnetic Hotspots for Highly Sensitive and Reproducible SERS Detection

matches.rationale: The abstract establishes core/satellite superstructures, coupled plasmon modes, and SERS hotspots, but it does not report a solution-versus-dried comparison or an interaction between measurement context and architecture.

matches.rationale: The record reports control of interparticle gaps and coupling to increase SERS intensity. It establishes spacing and hotspot-related components but does not address solution versus dried contexts or their dependence on the claimed architecture.
matches.title: Application of gold nanoparticles–epoxy surface nanocomposites for controlling hotspot density on a large surface area for SERS applications

matches.rationale: The record discusses three-dimensional plasmonic SERS platforms and hotspot density, which are components of the claimed subject matter. It does not establish context-dependent effects involving solution, drying, satellite architecture, or analyte redistribution.

matches.rationale: The abstract discusses SERS measurement conditions, analyte solubility, accessibility, and density near substrates. It does not link those variables to an Ag shell-coated core-satellite architecture or establish a solution-versus-dried conditional effect.
matches.title: Quantitative Surface-Enhanced Spectroscopy
